Wal-Flu is Walgreens' (American drugstore/pharmacy/apothecary) generic brand of the major brand's "flu/cold make you feel better" cocktails. It's only got 3 ingredients - it ain't even the strongest stuff we've got!

Here are the active ingredients that go into this kind of product. Look for them separately or mixed in things you can get ahold of:

Drug Name US Brand Name Use
Acetaminophen / Paracetamol Tylenol Fever reducer, pain reducer
Guaifenesin Mucinex / Robitussin Makes wracking dry coughs into nice wet ones (helps get mucous out) ("Expectorant")
Diphenhydramine Benadryl Anti-allergy, sleep aid, mild anti-nausea
Dextromethorphan Mucinex DM Cough suppressant
Pseudoephedrine Sudafed Decongestant. This is the one you can use to make meth, so it's only sold over-the-counter in the US (not off-the-shelf), and they require photo ID to purchase. It is the most effective oral decongestant.
Phenylephrine Sudafed PE Decongestant. Cannot be used to make meth, sold off-the-shelf.
Doxylamine NyQuil Anti-allergy, sleep aid
Fluticasone propionate Flonase Anti-allergy. This is a nasal spray of steroids. It opens your sinuses right up, even when oral medications don't work. Off-label use for cold/flu congestion.
Triamcinolone acetonide Nasacort Anti-allergy corticosteroid, similar use to fluticasone. Off-label for cold/flu congestion.

In the US, there are many products that mix lots of these together. Wal-Flu contains 3 ingredients:

  1. Acetaminophen/Paracetmol: Fever & pain reducer
  2. Diphenydramine: Anti-allergy, sleep aid (they call it a 'cough suppressant' because yeah, when you're asleep, you don't cough...)
  3. Phenylephrine: Decongestant

But why stop there? Tylenol's multi-symptom severe contains four:

  1. Acetaminophen/Paracetamol: Fever & pain reducer
  2. Dextromethorphan: Cough suppressant
  3. Guaifenesin: Expectorant ("no dry coughs")
  4. Phenylephrine: Decongestant

Point being, they're generally safe to mix-and-match, so if you can find the pieces, you can make your own Wal-Flu.

You're absolutely right that these cocktails can turn a person with bad allergies or a cold right around. Just watch your liver with the paracetamol...

And don't forget your multivitamin or vitamin-C supplement to get the placebo effect going ;)

P.S. Lemsip is primarily a large dose of Paracetamol and a bit of phenylephrine (non-meth decongestant). You're missing the cough medications and stronger decongestants.

P.P.S. I can do this with anti-allergy meds, too, but the TL;DR is cetirizine or fexofenadine for allergy season, and a spot of diphenhydramine during a short-term flare-up.
